items.title: Malaysia Airlines Overtakes AirAsia on India Routes by Standing Still
items.summary: AirAsia’s fuel-driven retreat should be a gift to its rivals, but high fuel costs and scarce aircraft mean few can afford to take advantage. Malaysia Airlines has overtaken it on India routes with 1% more seats in a market that shrank 10%. The longer AirAsia stays small, the more

items.title: Ras Al Khaimah Airport Courts Wynn’s Jet Set but Waits on Airlines
items.summary: Ras Al Khaimah’s airport is betting on Wynn’s new integrated resort and other luxury hotels to bring in five-star travelers. For now, it is upgrading the terminal it has and holding the new one until airlines commit. The resort’s delay pushes any payoff to late 2027.

items.title: Japan Is Closing in on the U.S. as High Costs and Politics Deter Travelers, Brand USA Says
items.summary: Research shows the U.S. losing ground to Japan as costs and politics turn travelers away. Brand USA is betting the lost demand is deferred, not gone, but its budget to win it back is shrinking.

items.title: Spirit’s $10 Million Data Sale to Google Clears Hurdle as Unions Win Privacy Protections
items.summary: If the sale clears, Google gets about 1.9 billion Spirit emails and 30 million lines of code to train its AI models, for $10 million. The unions’ win means employee data will be scrubbed first.

items.title: Aman Confirms Its Secret Third Brand Is Atma, Opening in Miami in 2031
items.summary: Aman has confirmed what the paper trail suggested to Skift in January. The open question is delivery: Janu, the group's second brand, has one hotel open after more than six years since its launch.

items.title: OpenAI Acquires Odessia, the AI Travel Agent From Sonder’s Co-Founder
items.summary: OpenAI didn't acquire Odessia for its revenue. It bought a team that built a working AI travel agent in months, plus a founder who ran a lodging company, which included hotels and short-term rentals, for a decade. It's a sign ChatGPT wants to do more in travel than send

items.title: Prices Prop Up Travel as Demand Cools
items.summary: Travel interest is slipping, but revenue is holding because prices are doing the work. That cushion only lasts as long as travelers keep paying more, which makes falling search activity worth watching closely heading into 2027.

items.title: ‘Is This Hilton?’ An Ad Blitz Answers: Yes, We Have Lifestyle Hotels
items.summary: Hilton spent years buying and licensing non-traditional hotel brands. Its new ad campaign is the bill coming due: It has to teach travelers about the new places to stay.
